source.text: እስመ፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ *ኢአመነ፡ ወኢሰባሕነ፡ ለስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ [ወኢሰባሕናሁ፡ ለእግዚእነ፡] ወተስፋነ፡ ኮነ፡ ዲበ፡ በትረ፡ መንግሥት*ነ፡ ወዲበ፡ ስብሐቲነ።
source.note: Charles1906 printed p.116/PDF154, verse7 only. Negative prefixes and source brackets checked against scan; full chapter remains held.

translation.text: For before him we did not believe, and we did not praise the name of the Lord of Spirits, [and we did not praise our Lord,][a] and our hope was in the scepter[b] of our kingdom and in our glory.

footnotes.text: Charles identifies this bracketed clause as dittography in printed p.116 note 5. It is retained in brackets here rather than presented as an uncontested part of the text.
Scepter can also be rendered staff or rod; the royal image is retained.

scope: Selected printed source negative prefixes and glyphs corrected; explicit dittography note and unique footnote anchors. Running English wording otherwise retained.

translation.text: And from it I said: blessed is the man who dies righteous and good, upon whom no book of wrongdoing has been written, and for whom no day of judgment will be found.

translation.text: And when they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned back[c] so as to flee from before his face; and that watercourse[a] gathered together, and it became swift according to its nature, and it filled with water and rose up until it covered those wolves.[b][d]

footnotes.text: Or 'that channel of water' or 'that torrent-bed'; the Ge'ez term likely refers to a stream-course that suddenly swells.
Or 'rose up to cover those wolves.' The final phrase may refer either to the flood reaching the wolves' covering/shelter or to the waters covering the wolves themselves.
Or 'as far as the covering of those wolves'.

scope: Mechanical removal of duplicated opening and trailing clauses; all surviving running words preserved. Existing lexical notes only reanchored, not independently certified.
